subject: Urgent: Production latency & error surge — Cumulus Health
messages:
From: Lenora Jacobs <lenora@cumulushealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: api-ops@cumulushealth.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jan 2028 11:14:02 -05:00
Subject: Production - tokens failing / massive latency spike

Markus —

We started seeing a sharp spike in request latencies to Redwood generation endpoints at ~10:58 EST and then a rising error rate (502/504) across our production pods. This is impacting our billing and scheduling workflows in the app. Error rates jumped from ~0.5% to >14% and p95 latencies moved from ~220ms to 4-6s.

We pasted a short sample of timestamps and request ids below, and attached our side logs. We rely on your platform for SLA — this is currently causing patient scheduling delays. Please treat as P1 and loop in network/ops.

Sample: 2028-01-09T15:01:02Z req=ch-xx-884 -> 504

Attachments: cumulus_error_log.txt (excerpt)

Can you confirm whether this is a Redwood regression or something on the peering/VPC side?

Lenora
Director of Platform Engineering
Cumulus Health
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jan 2028 08:20:31 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Production - tokens failing / massive latency spike

Following up from Lenora — P1 for Cumulus (DL-5932). Rishi/Monica: can you take point on triage? Immediate asks:
- Confirm whether we see node-level saturation, queue backpressure, or external path failures.
- Capture packet traces and DNS latencies for the affected region (us-central1) and attach pcap.
- Check our VPC peering logs and any recent changes to egress NAT/firewall rules.

I am starting a quick channel with Cumulus. I will update Lenora within 30 minutes with an interim summary.

Thanks — Markus
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jan 2028 08:44:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production - tokens failing / massive latency spike

Quick diagnostics summary (initial):
- Observed transient VPC peering route flap between our serving subnet and Cumulus VPC beginning 10:56:22 EST; BGP withdraw and re-advertise pattern for ~7 minutes. See vpc-peering-trace.txt.
- Concurrently DNS query latencies spiked on the customer-facing resolver set (200+ms to 1s) for redwood api hostnames; cache misses amplified latency.
- No GPU queue saturation on our nodes; per-node CPU/net looks normal. Errors correlate to TCP resets and TLS handshake timeouts, consistent with mid-path drops.

Attached: packet_capture.pcap (selected syn/retrans sequences), vpc-peering-trace.txt, short grep of proxy logs.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Enabled route pinning to fallback peering path for the affected size class.
- Pinned connections to alternate DNS resolver pool for Cumulus CIDR.

Will continue capture and coordinate with GCP NOC for root cause. Recommend we alert execs and offer a short credit while we stabilize.

-Rishi
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Lenora Jacobs <lenora@cumulushealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jan 2028 09:12:43 -08:00
Subject: RE: Production - tokens failing / massive latency spike

Lenora —

Thanks for the quick report and the logs. Short update: our SRE team has identified a transient route flap on the VPC peering path combined with elevated DNS latencies that together produced the observed error and latency spike. We applied immediate mitigations (route pinning + alternate DNS pool) at 09:04 PT; error rates started falling after ~4–6 minutes and we are monitoring.

Next steps we are taking:
- Full packet capture and timeline (shared) — attached.
- Engaging GCP Network Ops to review peering stability (we copied them).
- Post-incident RCA targeted for 72 hours with corrective actions (BGP hold timers, peering config validation, improved pref failover).
- Temporary credit: we will propose a partial credits package to the account owner; Sean (cc'd) will review for executive sign-off.

I apologize for the impact; we know this is sensitive for scheduling systems. We will share the postmortem and mitigations when ready. If you want a call now, I can get the SRE and network folks on the line.

-Markus
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: packet_capture.pcap (selected), vpc-peering-trace.txt
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Lenora Jacobs <lenora@cumulushealth.com>, markus_klein@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jan 2028 15:47:06 -08:00
Subject: RE: Production - tokens failing / massive latency spike

Lenora / Cumulus team —

First, thank you for flagging this and for the patience while our teams worked through the path issue. I reviewed the SRE notes and the packet captures; this was a mid-path peering instability at the provider layer that manifested as a route flap and increased DNS lookup times. Our team has two asks while we complete the RCA:

1) We will draft a courtesy credit to offset the impact to you for the affected window (I will follow up with the finance/sales team and share the proposal by EOD tomorrow).
2) Request a joint 30-minute post-incident call with your network and platform engineers + our serving/runtime and networking PMs; propose 2028-01-11 10:00 ET.

We are treating this with executive attention and will ensure the RCA includes actionable items both on our side (peering resilience, DNS caching improvements) and recommendations for BGP/peering configs.

If you need immediate escalation, reply-all and I will open the on-call bridge.

Regards — Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
